findings.title: Default signed-URL HMAC secret falls back to Administrator.creation (guest workflow impersonation)
findings.evidence: get_secret() returns frappe.local.conf.get('secret') or str(frappe.db.get_value('User','Administrator','creation')). No installer/update_site_config path ever provisions conf.secret (only encryption_key is auto-generated). hmac.new() is called without digestmod (MD5 on Py2/3.6/3.7). confirm_action is allow_guest=True: after verify_request() it does frappe.set_user(user) from signed query params then apply_workflow.
findings.attack_path: 1) On a default site with no site_config.secret, recover Administrator.creation (DB read, backup, or any existing SQLi). 2) Forge _signature over confirm_action params (action, doctype, docname, user=<victim>). 3) Guest GET/POST /api/method/frappe.workflow.doctype.workflow_action.workflow_action.confirm_action?...&_signature=... 4) Server set_user(victim) and applies the workflow transition.
findings.impact: Guest forges workflow approval/reject links and impersonates arbitrary users for workflow state changes. Same secret also signs personal-data deletion confirm and related verified_command links.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior near-miss treated verify_request HMAC as a solid gate. This is a crypto/secrets break of that gate: default key is a DB timestamp, never auto-provisioned as a random secret, and MD5 HMAC. Distinct from unsigned newsletter confirmed_unsubscribe.

findings.title: CSRF validation skipped for device=mobile sessions while sid cookie auth remains
findings.evidence: Login stores self.device = frappe.form_dict.get('device') or 'desktop' into session data. validate_csrf_token returns early when session.data.device=='mobile' (also when csrf_token missing). CookieManager.set_cookie writes sid without HttpOnly/SameSite/Secure. POST/PUT still commit via after_request.
findings.attack_path: 1) Victim uses Frappe mobile/device=mobile login (or any client POSTing device=mobile). 2) Attacker page issues credentialed cross-site POST to /api/method/<any whitelist> without X-Frappe-CSRF-Token. 3) Server skips CSRF check and executes as the victim (e.g. set_value, delete, update_document_title, get_email_template SSTI).
findings.impact: Full CSRF against mobile-device cookie sessions: any state-changing whitelisted method runs as the victim, chaining into already-known critical sinks.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not in the stored 52 findings or prompt already-reported injection list. CSRF was an explicit remaining sink. Distinct from ignore_csrf site_config and from GET-only no-commit quirks.

findings.title: Password-reset keys generated with non-CSPRNG random.choice (MT19937)
findings.evidence: random_string uses from random import choice over ascii_letters+digits. reset_password sets reset_password_key = random_string(32) and emails /update-password?key=. generate_hash (sessions/api secrets) also seeds from random_string(8)+time.time().
findings.attack_path: 1) Observe MT19937 outputs from other random_string uses in the same process (e.g. uploaded filenames via get_random_filename). 2) Clone PRNG state. 3) Predict subsequent reset_password_key values after triggering reset_password for a target account. 4) Complete guest update_password with the predicted key.
findings.impact: Account takeover via predictable password-reset tokens when PRNG state can be recovered.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Crypto/secrets issue not previously stored. Distinct from update_document_title writing reset_password_key and from login_oauth_user email trust.

findings.title: OAuth client_secret truncated to 10 hex chars (~40 bits)
findings.evidence: If client_secret empty on save: self.client_secret = frappe.generate_hash(length=10). generate_hash returns sha224(...).hexdigest()[:10] — 16^10 ≈ 2^40 possibilities.
findings.attack_path: 1) Learn client_id (often public). 2) Offline/online brute-force the 40-bit client_secret. 3) Use the OAuth client credentials in token flows allowed for that client.
findings.impact: OAuth client impersonation / unauthorized token issuance for configured OAuth clients.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Not previously reported. Distinct from jwt.decode(verify=False) IdP near-miss and from Google Drive/Contacts OAuth token IDOR findings.

findings.title: LDAP TLS hardcodes PROTOCOL_TLSv1 (and CERT_NONE when trust disabled)
findings.evidence: ldap3.Tls(validate=CERT_REQUIRED or CERT_NONE, version=ssl.PROTOCOL_TLSv1) — TLS 1.0 only, regardless of server capability. require_trusted_certificate!='Yes' sets CERT_NONE.
findings.attack_path: 1) Site enables LDAP login. 2) Network attacker MITMs LDAP to the directory over TLS 1.0 (or plaintext-equivalent when CERT_NONE). 3) Recover bind credentials / user passwords during authenticate().
findings.impact: LDAP credential interception on any deployment using LDAP Settings.
findings.why_not_duplicate: Prior LDAP near-miss covered search-filter injection needing bind only. This is a separate crypto/transport weakness.
